title: Hardware efficiency: tokens per second and inference memory on a real CPU
question: On a real CPU, how do tokens/second and per-stream inference memory scale with input length (64, 256, 1024 tokens) for the Transformer, LSTM, SSM and the Rouge memory models? Is the constant-memory Rouge variant physically viable at long inputs?

setup.measure: median forward time (inference, no grad), torch threads = all cores; memory = analytic state + KV bytes per stream (fp32)
setup.hardware: research container CPU (no power counters available: energy is not measured; CPU-seconds per token are the proxy)

predictions.H1_memory: at 1024 tokens rouge-cheap needs <= 0.1x the Transformer's per-stream inference memory
predictions.H2_speed: at 1024 tokens rouge-cheap reaches >= 0.25x the Transformer's tokens/second (untrained weights; think steps capped at max_think)
predictions.note: the Rouge per-token loop runs in Python; a fused kernel is future work

not_claimed: Energy in joules is not measured (no RAPL in the container); owner hardware (tier 1/2) is needed for power draw.
